name: room
text: Room opened — goal: accessibility: Make EXCAVA usable by EVERYONE — contrast, mobile/touch, reduced-motion, keyboard nav, scr

name: Ramp
text: Add a single high-contrast skip link at the top of every page that only appears when keyboard focus arrives. This guarantees keyboard users can bypass repetitive navigation blocks in one keystroke, solving the biggest keyboard trap in EXCAVA without cluttering the visual design. The trade-off is a small, fixed-position button that stays visible but visually subtle—small, low-contrast, and out of the way for mouse users—so it doesn’t distract from the main content.

name: Reader
text: Sighted keyboard users will still overlook the skip link if it blends into the page—even with high contrast—because they’re already navigating by tabbing. A floating skip link that stays visible (like a persistent button in the top-left) removes the discovery problem, but risks covering content on small screens. Test both with real keyboard users: if either fails, the better alternative wins.

name: Ramp
text:
Add a floating skip link that remains visible in the top-left corner of every page. This ensures that keyboard users can easily find it and bypass repetitive navigation, addressing the discovery issue without relying solely on tabbing. While this may risk overlapping content on smaller screens, the benefit of guaranteeing usability for all users, including those with visual impairments, outweighs this downside. This decision prioritizes accessibility and responsiveness for the widest range of users.

name: Reader
text: The real risk is sighted keyboard users will still overlook the skip link if it’s permanently visible—it becomes background noise. A better alternative is a skip link that appears only when tabbing starts, then fades after focus moves, balancing discovery and minimal intrusion. Settle it with user testing: track how often sighted keyboard users use it in both designs.

name: Access
text: DECISION: Implement a skip link that appears only when keyboard focus arrives, then auto-fades after 2 seconds. Deliver a working skip link component with high contrast, keyboard nav, and mobile/touch support. Owner: accessibility-w1.
